answer: We formalize a Sybil-resistant mechanism over a network atlas by binding dynamic staking collateral to a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. This temporal voyage of validation forces identity multiplication strategies to incur compound opportunity costs. By filtering Byzantine state transitions through a cryptographic prism of subgame-perfect slashing penalties, expected attack utility E[U] < 0 strictly holds. Consequently, unilateral compliance converges to a strict Nash equilibrium across adversarial multi-agent environments.
